title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the third version of 'Analysis situs' (June 1986), Grothendieck sets up an axiomatic theory of 'ateliers'. These are categories or lattices of 'figures' in a tame-topology setting, with: a refinement order ≤; an internal-refinement relation ≪; a disjointness/compatibility relation ∥; strata ('strates'); and 'lieux' (loci), meaning the restriction F ↦ F_L of a figure to a locus L. The previous page proves lemmas of the form 'for x ∈ Comb(Q), x_P = ∅ ⇔ x ∉ Comb(P)' and 'for P ≤ Q, F ≪ Q: F_P = ∅ ⇔ F ∥ P' (the latter using At D). Those lemmas lead to introducing a new axiom here.

The new axiom is At CL(pol): the compatibility criterion via loci for polyhedral cells, alongside the spatial version At CL(spac). The page then records the logical dependencies between the 'compatibility–disposition' axioms:
(a) At L2 + At CL(spac or pol) ⇔ At L2 + At C(spac or pol). Given the disposition criterion via loci, the locus-wise compatibility criterion is equivalent to the ordinary compatibility criterion.
(b) At D0 + At L1 (divisibility) + At CL(spac/pol) ⇒ At L2.
(c) At L2 + At L3 ⇒ At D ⇒ At D0. D0 means ∥ is stable under ≪.
(d) At L3 + At CL(spac) ⇒ At C. The added arrow shows At C ⇒ At D, completing the chain C ⇒ D ⇒ D0.
(e) At D ⇒ At L3. Hence L2 + L3 ⇔ L2 + D.

The summary he retains is the hierarchy C ⇒ D ⇒ D0, with D (and C) implying [L1], L2, L3. It covers the variants At C(spac), At C(pol), At CL(spac), At CL(pol).

Remark 1: the unconditional locus axioms L2 and L3 give D, hence D0, but not C. To obtain C from axioms about loci one needs At CL(spac) or At CL(pol).

Conclusion: At L2 + At L3 + At CL(spac) implies all compatibility–disposition axioms (spatial style):
- At C(spac) by (a);
- At D by (c), hence D0;
- At C by (d).

A crossed-out final line says one can put 'pol' instead of 'spac'. The next page repackages this: L1+L2+L3+CL ⇔ D0+L1+L3+CL ⇒ D+L1+CL+C. It also gives the full list of axioms At1–At7, C, D, D0, Fil, L1–L3, CL.

Purpose: a minimal, economical axiom system for a 'tame topology' (topologie modérée) of stratified figures, as envisaged in Esquisse d'un programme §5–6.
errors: No genuine logical error is visible. Combining (b) and (c) gives D0+L1+L3+CL ⇒ L2 ⇒ (with L3) D ⇒ D0, so the equivalence on the next page is consistent. (e) D ⇒ L3 makes L2+L3 ⇔ L2+D, which is consistent with (c).

The first line of relations is crossed out ('At D0 + At L1 + At CL(spac) ⇔ At L2 ⇒ At D'). It was replaced by the more careful (a)–(e). The crossed-out claim of equivalence was too strong: D0+L1+CL only implies L2 (b), not conversely without further axioms.
In (a), a crossed-out '⇏ At D0' indicates he first considered, then dropped, a non-implication claim.

ideas.what: Axiomatic framework of 'ateliers' (spatial/polyhedral) for tame topology, with figures, refinement ≤, internal refinement ≪, disjointness ∥, strata and loci
ideas.modern_name: axiomatic tame topology; closest analogues are o-minimal structures and abstract stratified / PL categories
ideas.usually_credited_to: o-minimality: van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight (1980s); the 'atelier' axiomatics itself is unpublished Grothendieck
ideas.where_published: Only the programme is sketched in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5–6 'topologie modérée'; the 1986 Analysis situs notes are unpublished

ideas.what: Dependency analysis among axioms: C ⇒ D ⇒ D0; L2+L3 ⇒ D; D ⇒ L3; D0+L1+CL ⇒ L2; L3+CL ⇒ C; L2+CL ⇔ L2+C; hence L2+L3+CL(spac) suffices for all compatibility–disposition axioms
ideas.modern_name: reduction of an axiom system / independence bookkeeping

ideas.what: Compatibility criterion 'by loci' (At CL): compatibility of refinements tested after restriction to loci, in spatial and polyhedral versions
ideas.modern_name: local (stratum/locus-wise) criterion for common refinement, akin to local-to-global checks in stratified spaces

missed.claim: The 'atelier' axiomatics for tame topology, including its locus axioms (L1–L3, CL), was never published or taken up. This page shows a worked-out minimal axiom set (L2 + L3 + CL, plus L1 for divisibility) generating all compatibility/disposition axioms. It is an explicit, unexplored alternative to o-minimal axiomatics.
missed.quote: At L2 + At L3 + At CL(spac) implique tous les axiomes de compatibilité-disposition (style spac)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Comparing it with o-minimal structures, Shiota's tame categories, or Clausen–Scholze-style tame/condensed approaches could show whether Grothendieck's locus-based axioms give a genuinely different foundation for 'topologie modérée'. The page itself is bookkeeping, so its independent value is modest.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is internal bookkeeping of logical dependencies among unpublished axioms. It is interesting only as evidence of how far the 1986 tame-topology axiomatics was carried. There is no standalone new result.
transcription_corrections: 'Voir dingue ce fait p. 45' is probably 'Voir digression faite p. 45' (reading uncertain).

'axiomes de compatibilité-disjonction' should likely read 'compatibilité-disposition', consistent with the next page ('axiomes de compatibilité, disposition'; At D = 'critère de disposition'). The same applies to 'les deux axiomes L2, L3 de disposition'.

Remark 1 reads roughly: 'Du point de vue des axiomes inconditionnels (spac ou pol ...), les deux axiomes L2, L3 de disposition impliquent D donc D0, mais non C (axiome de compatibilité ...). Pour nous assurer C d'axiomes pertinents sur les lieux, il nous faut des At CL spac ou At CL(pol).'
At the bottom right, 'At C par NB ...' is likely 'At C par (d)', given the preceding '(a)', '(c) d'où D0'.
Crossed-out last line: probably 'On peut remplacer dans ... At L ... "pol" ald [au lieu de] "spac"'.
In (d), the handwritten double arrow points from At C toward At D, i.e. At C ⇒ At D.
